(Question) I switch to Elementary Os how can i install Nvidia drivers

The great thing about Linux is this stuff is generally super easy. First thing make sure you open a terminal and type

sudo apt-get upgrade

And that will make sure you're all updated. Next click on the applications button in the top left of the screen and search for "additional drivers". Click on the driver you want and you should be good to go.

If you're still getting black screened you'll probably need more detailed instructions than I can give (reasonably) on my phone. Try the Ubuntu forums, they're super helpful and most of the advice should translate well between elementary os and Ubuntu.

Edit: generally installing drivers and programs from their websites is a bad idea. Try to get them through a command line instruction or the app store if possible.

I'd just like to mention that you should do:

'sudo apt-get update'

before you do:

'sudo apt-get upgrade'

update gets the list of all the new programs available and upgrade installs them. After having done that, you can do what the parent says or type:

'sudo apt-get install nividia-current'

to install the latest stable nvidia drivers. After the above commands are run, you will have to follow on screen instructions and confirm that you want to install the selected programs and their dependencies.

edit: elementary os is based on ubuntu so you can usually follow the same guides as ubuntu. The same commands should work but the windows might look a bit different.

You dont want to become a hamplanet by eating 1200? Sry to say but you should aim to eat your BMR, especially when you are in bed all day long. By eating 1200 your healthy body will start starvation mode. As you are in bed (and thus not using your muscles) your body will prioritize burning muscles instead of fat (as the former isn't used, while the latter is needed to survive). If you intend to eat below your bmr, try to minimize the deficit. The higher the caloric deficit, the bigger the share of muscles that is consumed by your body. -> small deficits (if any) while in bed. Work out after your stay to restore the lost muscular mass. This way you can prevent the yoyo-effect from happening.

The key to staying healthy is to maintain balance between your caloric intake and your energy comsumption (with muscles being the most important dynamic factor in this equation). The no1 mistake obeasts make, is to go on a crash diet that results in loosing all their muscular mass and thus, lowering their BMR to ridiculous amounts. When they stop "dieting" and eat "normally" again, their lowered BMR leads to weight gain that exceeds their initial weight.

It's not a question of "believing" something, but rather of examining and testing a plan. If someone lays out their actual plan for how they would accomplish something they are claiming they want to do, then you can compare their plan to things people have tried in the past, you can test whether things they claim would perform in a certain way were capable of doing so, you can break down their claimed budget for getting something done and figure out if it is really possible to do it at that price, and so on. The difference between campaigning and governing is that you actually need to do real-world things when you're governing.
